title: Exact derived continuous scalar localization and raw fraction descent
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and let $\varpi$ be a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with a specified map from the constant ring sheaf $A_{\mathcal S}$, and put $S=R[1/\varpi]$ by sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves, sheaf tensor products and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in universes in which these exist. Scalar actions on module morphisms are multiplication by constant sections and on derived morphisms are their induced actions [def-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-coefficient-actions]. The $E=A[1/\varpi]$ action on $D(S)$ is given by the localized constant sections. Let $\mathcal C$ be any full $A$-linear triangulated subcategory of $D(R)$, with the induced linear shifts [def-weil-linear-functor, def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ be the raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], whose distinguished triangles are the triangles isomorphic to images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal C$.

The actual scalar functor $T(M)=S\otimes_R M$, $T(f)=1\otimes f$, is additive and exact. The derived scalar extension $F=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is naturally isomorphic, as a triangulated $A$-linear functor, to the termwise exact derived functor $D(T)$. For every complex $K$ and every K-flat resolution $P\to K$, the comparison is the derived isomorphism represented by $T(P)\to T(K)$. In degree zero it is the ordinary scalar extension. There are natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^r(FK)\cong S\otimes_R\mathcal H^r(K)$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], induced by the cycle and boundary identifications, natural for all derived morphisms. In particular every cohomological vanishing interval is preserved.

The formulas $\overline F(QK)=FK$ and $\overline F(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F(f)$ determine an $E$-linear triangulated functor $\overline F:\mathcal C[1/\varpi]\to D(S)$ factoring $F|_{\mathcal C}$. The fraction formula is independent of representatives: whenever $\varpi^t(\varpi^m f-\varpi^n g)=0$ for some $t\geq0$, its two images agree. It preserves addition, identities, composition and multiplication by every scalar $a/\varpi^m\in E$. Its shift comparison has components those of $F$ and is natural on fraction morphisms; on the image of an integral distinguished triangle its image is the distinguished triangle obtained by applying $F$. No boundedness or constructibility hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ or its objects is imposed.

proof.text: Define the descended functor on each raw tensor Hom by the balanced additive map b tensor f ↦ eE(b) F(f). Tensor induction proves identities, composition, additivity and E-linearity. For the representative relation, apply F, cancel the unit image of t^k, and multiply by t^(-(n+m)); this gives equality of the displayed fraction images, including torsion and zero-ring cases. At denominator one the comparison is the identity natural isomorphism.

source.place: Assembly of Tags 015F and 05R6, Homology 010N and sheaf localization 03ET; explicit raw fraction calculation for the functor in Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2).

proof.text: Use the proof of lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated with its induced shifts in every integer degree, retaining the definitional formula for all shifts. The tensor-Hom comparison with rationalization proves the raw functor Q is a localization. Descend the shift comparison of F through Q; its components reduce to those of F because the comparison for Q and the denominator-one factorization are identities. A distinguished raw triangle is isomorphic to Q of an integral distinguished triangle, whose image under the descended functor is distinguished. Thus the explicit fraction functor is triangulated.
